name: Pillars
overview: Scripture presents pillars as significant memorials and symbols of divine encounters, as seen when Jacob set up a stone pillar anointed with oil at Bethel, marking God's presence and a solemn vow (Genesis 28:18; 31:13). Pillars also served as tangible witnesses in covenant agreements, exemplified by Laban and Jacob's heap and pillar acting as a boundary and testimony to their pact (Genesis 31:51-52). Additionally, pillars can represent both judgment and remembrance, such as Lot's wife becoming a pillar of salt, and Jacob erecting a pillar at Rachel's grave as a lasting memorial (Genesis 19:26; 35:20). These examples underscore pillars as enduring symbols of God's work, faithfulness, and the seriousness of His covenants.
